clue.text: Nothing to be said, on the face of it

definitions.text: Nothing to be said, on the face of it

parts.words: Nothing to be said, on the face of it
parts.note: a face that says nothing at all, giving away no feeling, is read as one lacking any look of feeling

explanation.definitionFit: A blank, deadpan face shows no feeling, so the face itself 'says' nothing.

clue.text: Betrays a former spouse's mannerisms

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
poses are affected attitudes or mannerisms

explanation.surface: Someone's divorced partner gives away their irritating habits.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray a secret or a person is to reveal or unmask them.

clue.text: You must be kidding, surely!

parts.note: the whole clue is a cry of disbelief, and the answer is the stock British phrase said to someone suspected of teasing

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is short for 'pull the other one, it's got bells on', a British retort to an obvious tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a stock retort meaning 'I don't believe you, you're joking'.

clue.text: Casca's deadly sin?

parts.note: Casca, a conspirator in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, is among those said to have struck Caesar out of jealousy, one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.walkthrough: At the end of Julius Caesar, Antony says all the conspirators except Brutus acted 'in envy of great Caesar'; Casca struck first.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy of another's success is one of the seven deadly sins, and the motive Shakespeare gives Casca.

clue.text: Example arboreal neatness

definitions.meaning: an example of a tree, a conifer
the second sense is the adjective meaning smart and trim, standing for the quality of being neat

explanation.surface: A tree that is a model of tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a noun in the clue, but the answer in that sense is an adjective (smart, trim); the setter stretches the part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a conifer tree, and as an adjective means smartly turned out and trim.

clue.text: One causing displeasure being close in tender embrace

indicators.note: embrace means the word for tender wraps its arms around the word for close

parts.note: to tender is to offer
a close is an end

explanation.surface: Someone annoying others by getting near in an affectionate hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' and 'in' are linking words; the verb 'tender' (to offer formally) is disguised by its sense of gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives offence causes displeasure to others.

clue.text: Extended run in the business

parts.note: a lengthy stretch spent working in one trade or profession, though 'run' suggests a show's run

explanation.definitionFit: Many years spent working in a profession amount to a lengthy working life.

clue.text: Round flight

parts.note: a flight of steps that winds round and round, though 'flight' suggests air travel

explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps that winds around a central column is a helical set of stairs.

clue.text: Babe in the Wood"

parts.note: one of the two children abandoned in the forest in the Grimm fairy tale with the gingerbread house

explanation.walkthrough: The Babes in the Wood is a separate English tale, but the phrase fits the sister in Hansel's story, lost in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the girl lost in the forest with her brother Hansel in the Grimm fairy tale.

clue.text: Mate to maintain is a time-consuming business

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
to aver is to maintain or assert

explanation.surface: A friend insisting on a point drags things out.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or long-winded rigmarole wastes a great deal of time.

clue.text: His interest is of the more impressive kind

definitions.text: His interest is of the more impressive kind

parts.words: His interest is of the more impressive kind
parts.note: read one way, a hobbyist who keeps a particular interest (pigeons, dogs); read another, the comparative 'more elaborate'

explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon or dog breeder is a devotee of a hobby, and the same word is the comparative of 'elaborate'.

clue.text: Original sinner's offspring said to be old-fashioned

indicators.note: said signals that the archaic form is spoken out loud and gives a different spelling

parts.note: saith is the archaic, Biblical form of 'says'

explanation.surface: A child of the first wrongdoer is supposedly a fuddy-duddy.
explanation.walkthrough: The original sinner is Adam, whose third son was born after Cain and Abel; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this third son was born to Adam, the first man to sin.

clue.text: By altering Colin's coat he spoils the image

indicators.note: altering tells us to rearrange the letters of the named man's coat

explanation.surface: A man who ruins Colin's jacket also ruins his look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altering' rearranges the ten letters of COLIN'S COAT; 'By' is a link. The definition plays on images as religious icons.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a breaker of religious images, now anyone who attacks cherished beliefs.

clue.text: Diversifying link in season doesn't amount to much

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the season

parts.note: spring is a season

indicators.note: diversifying varies the order of the letters of link

explanation.surface: Varying a connection during a time of year makes little difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diversifying' turns LINK into INKL, which 'in' puts inside SPRING after SPR.
explanation.definitionFit: A light scattering is a small quantity, something that is not much.

clue.text: Dropping off one of Snow White's retinue

definitions.meaning: one of the seven dwarfs in the Disney film of the fairy tale

explanation.definitionFit: Drowsiness when nodding off, and the name of the yawning dwarf in the Disney film.

clue.text: Rare slip can cause such a comeback

indicators.note: can cause tells us the two words produce a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: An uncommon mistake can provoke retaliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can cause' rearranges the letters of RARE SLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaliation is a hitting back, a return blow for an injury.

clue.text: Tie-up for E. Kent resort

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, means the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A link-up arranged for a seaside town in East Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but is re-sort, the signal to rearrange FOR E KENT. Kent is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a square knot used to tie two ropes together.

clue.text: Talked persistently and made a sale

definitions.meaning: to retail gossip is to tell it over and over
sold goods in a shop, to the public

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to recount repeatedly, and to sell goods to the public in a shop.

clue.text: Suffering from one bear's affection

indicators.note: suffering from suggests the pieces are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
bear's, with its s, gives the word bears

explanation.surface: A sickness caught from a single bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering from' rearranges I and BEARS. 'Affection' is used in its old medical sense of a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: In old medical usage an affection is a disease, and this is a viral disease spread by bites.

clue.text: State of a number in the grasp of the Leningrad banker

indicators.note: in the grasp of means held inside the river's name

parts.note: a banker is a river (it has banks); the Neva runs through Leningrad, now St Petersburg
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: The financial condition of a figure held by a Soviet bank manager.
explanation.walkthrough: A and D go into NEVA after NEV. 'Banker' meaning river is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Cicero's friend finds room at the top with us

parts.note: an attic is a room right at the top of a house
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend of the Roman orator discovers a loft with us in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Pomponius Atticus was Cicero's lifelong friend and correspondent; 'finds' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Atticus was the close friend to whom the Roman orator wrote many surviving letters.

clue.text: Edible titbit that may be copied, apparently

parts.note: may in the sense 'is able to' gives can
to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: A party snack that could be imitated, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that may be copied' is read as CAN APE; 'be' and 'apparently' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A small savoury on bread or a biscuit served with drinks is a titbit.

clue.text: When up to it, suddenly it dawns on one

definitions.text: When up to it, suddenly it dawns on one

parts.words: When up to it, suddenly it dawns on one
parts.note: read as daybreak arriving: when you are up at that hour, day dawns, though 'it dawns on one' suggests sudden realisation

explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is when the first light appears, as the day dawns.

clue.text: Worry about mist from the sea

definitions.meaning: a sea mist drifting inland, especially on England's east coast

explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link. The second sense is a regional British word, a sea mist coming in off the North Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to be anxious, and the noun is a regional word for a coastal fog.

clue.text: Holes in one

parts.note: in golf a hole completed in a single stroke has a slang name shared with top playing cards

explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a hole completed with one stroke is called by the name of the top playing card.

clue.text: Feeling of initial energy at a formal proposal

indicators.note: initial tells us to take only the first letter of energy

parts.note: a motion is a formal proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A sense of early vigour when a proposal is tabled.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a strong feeling such as joy or anger.

clue.text: Rocking chair in a hundred no longer in use

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the other pieces

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters of chair into a new order

explanation.surface: A rocking chair in a hundred households has gone out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocking' turns CHAIR into RCHAI, which 'in' puts between A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Something antiquated has fallen out of use and belongs to an earlier age.

clue.text: Does it keep spaceman in a buoyant mood?

definitions.text: Does it keep spaceman in a buoyant mood?

parts.words: Does it keep spaceman in a buoyant mood?
parts.note: an astronaut floating free of gravity is literally buoyant, though the phrase suggests a cheerful mood

explanation.definitionFit: In orbit astronauts float about, having no apparent heaviness.
